page0.text:
She looks up at the clock on the wall, the ticking of the second hand ringing keenly in her ears.
The time is past 4:00 PM.
School got out a long time ago, and it's well past the time he would've gotten home, even if he stopped for groceries.
"...Senpai's late. I wonder why."
She whispers dreamily, leaning against the wall.

page1.text:
"Huh...?"
She moves slowly, feeling dizzy thanks to her fever.
She's slightly surprised by her own voice.
The clock ticking sounds so loud it grates on her ears, yet she can't hear her own voice very well.
That simple noise alone keeps resonating in her earlobes.
The steady tick-tock rhythm of the clock,
and the badump of her heart, straining to pump blood.
The two sounds get into her head even if she covers her ears, making the dizziness worse.

page2.text:
"That's weird...I was sure I got over the cold."
That's why she sent the caretaker home.
Her temperature was normal when she measured it, and she managed to make lunch on her own.
In the afternoon, she felt like her usual self again, and she looked forward to seeing the real master of the house come home.

page3.text:
"It's hot..."
And yet, her whole body feels hot.
The heat isn't coming from herself, but someplace else.
Something between her blood vessels and overlapping muscles, in gaps that shouldn't be there.
Something other than herself penetrates deep inside, running like a car engine.
Her fever is so hot, so endless, so unlike anything she's ever experienced before, that she can't help but visualize it as such.

page4.text:
If you asked her whether it feels bizarre, whether it's uncomfortable, she'd say yes to both.
She isn't the only one who feels suffocated.
The things creeping between her blood vessels and nerves are having a hard time, too.
To use an example, they're like puppies trapped in a can full of ground meat, searching for an exit.
They're the real cause of her fever... The puppies wriggling in her body, desperately trying to fulfill their function.
She finds them adorable somehow, and can't bring herself to hate the sensation.

page5.text:
"The clock...is so loud..."
She absently stares at the clock.
It's now half past four.
Just a little longer. He's sure to be home in another thirty minutes.
Before then, she needs to calm her body down and quiet the things running throughout her body.

page6.text:
"It's okay...this has happened before..."
Yes, she's used to these symptoms.
She's experienced them many times since childhood, and she's been taught how to relieve them.
That's why she thinks she can calm this down. But the fever doesn't recede, and the things in her move even faster.

page7.text:
"No...something's wrong...Senpai..."
Her body won't relax.
Everything she's tried before doesn't work.
What is she missing? What does she need? What changed?
She desperately tries to figure it out, but the ticking is too distracting. She can't think straight.

page8.text:
"Huh...? This noise..."
Finally, she realizes that it isn't the clock, but an alarm emitted by the house itself.
"Well, well. Emiya isn't here. That's convenient."
Someone familiar appears before her, tracking dirt into the house.

page9.text:
"Shin...ji..."
"Hey now, what's wrong, Sakura? What are you doing all alone without Emiya? This must be the drawback from overusing Rider."
The man enters the living room and walks up to the girl slumped against the wall.

page10.text:
"Ah."
She can't put any strength into her muscles.
She never had the energy to move to begin with.

page11.text:
"I'm here to pick you up, Sakura. No more playing house."
He looks down on her with a plastic smile.
"Shinji..."
"Let's go. I'm going to settle the score with Emiya. You want to see him too, right? I'll give you a front-row seat."
The man grabs her arm and drags her to her feet.

page12.text:
"N-no, I don't want to...!"
She tries to free her arm, but she doesn't have the strength to even do that.
The man drags her along, putting on a pleasant front.

page13.text:
"Don't be so upset, Sakura. You should listen to your big brother."
"No...that's not what you promised! You said you wouldn't hurt Senpai!"
She protests tearfully.
It doesn't sway him.
It seems he's set on playing the caring brother, mouth drawn in a thin smile.

page14.text:
"Uuu..."
Sobs spill out from her.
"I care, you know. Grandpa gave me something, but I'd rather not use it."
The man pulls the girl outside by the arm.

page15.text:
"Ah..."
"Relax. We're just settling things, man to man. I'll keep my promise, and you can come back here once we're finished. It's just, I've gotta rake him over the coals a little bit for leaving my sister in such a sorry state."
The man whispers in a delighted tone, close enough for his lips to touch the girl's ear.

page16.text:
"...uuu..."
She closes her mouth.
She knows better than anyone that her brother won't listen to anyone once he's made up his mind.

page17.text:
"That's a good girl, Sakura. Let's get a step ahead of him. It wouldn't be good to wait here, and if we're going to play, I need to invite him to the base I prepared. Rider, bring Sakura."
The man passes the girl to a Servant, and leaves the living room.
"Ri...der..."
The girl looks up.
She sees a Servant with flowing hair, long enough to touch the ground.

page18.text:
"I'm home!"
I announce myself as I enter the house.
...
Suddenly,
I'm overcome by a sense of discomfort.

page19.text:
"Emiya, the hallway."
...
It's clear what caught her attention.
In the hallway are marks that look like footprints.
Only Sakura's shoes are out front.
I didn't see the caretaker's shoes, so they must have gone home.

page20.text:
"Sakura?"
I go to the guest bedroom.
Nobody's inside.
Discomfort turns to dread.

page21.text:
I go back to the living room.
Sakura isn't here, either.
The tracks in the hallway end in the living room.
Someone with dirty feet did something here and then went outside.

page22.text:
"...Emiya. Look at the floor.
The tracks end here."
"I know. Sakura was in here."
Yes, I know.
Sakura was here in the living room waiting for me to come home, and now she's gone.

page23.text:
There are unfamiliar footprints in the hallway.
That's all I know.
It's strange that I haven't deduced the situation.
The answer should be clear, once I take some time to think.

page24.text:
Calmly.
Calmly.
Calmly.
If I calm down and think, I'll figure out what happened here.
But why...
"..."
Why won't my brain work at all?

page25.text:
"Hey, Emiya!?"
...
I should have come home earlier.
I should have taken this more seriously.
Didn't I take Sakura in because I was afraid this would happen?
Zouken said that Sakura had nothing to do with this.
Why did I believe him?
As long as Sakura's one of the Matous, there's no way she isn't related.

page26.text:
So, why?
Why did I accept an explanation that was convenient for me, without questioning it at all!?

page27.text:
"..."
The telephone rings.
Tohsaka keeps quiet. I nod at her, and pick up the receiver.

page28.text:
"Hello? You finally home, Emiya?"
Shinji's the caller.
There's no doubt about it, and I was expecting this anyway.

page29.text:
"What did you do to Sakura?"
"Huh? I came to pick her up. She's my sister, so I can't leave her at some other guy's house."

page30.text:
"Shinji."
"Haha! Nice, you're getting pissed! I bet you're frustrated that I took her back!"
Tohsaka leans in close, as if she can hear what he's saying.
I keep her at a distance with one hand and continue the call.

page31.text:
"Enough beating around the bush. Tell me what you want."
"Heh! I bet you know. Let's settle things, Emiya. I bet you think we aren't finished yet, after last time."
"No, we are. You ran away. There's nothing left to settle."

page32.text: "You still don't get it! That was only because of the difference in our Servants, not you! I never would've run if you didn't have Saber! I never would've lost if Saber hadn't shown up!"

page33.text:
If Saber hadn't shown up?
...I see now.
It sounds like Rider hasn't told him that I lost Saber.
Yeah...that's why he came to take her back by force.
In other words, this phone call is...

page34.text:
"Shinji. What are you going to do with her?"
"Don't get all heavy on me, man. I won't do anything to my precious sister.
Not if you come to see me, alone."
"Rrgh!"
I hold off Tohsaka.
If she interrupts this conversation, it'll definitely go off the rails.

page35.text:
"You're telling me to fight you without Saber?"
"Nice, I'm glad you understand right away when it counts.
—Come to the school. Make sure you're alone. Rider's Bounded Field is on the school. If you bring Saber, I'll know right away.
Of course...I bet you wouldn't do anything so cowardly in front of Sakura."

page36.text: I hear snickering over the receiver.

page37.text:
"I'll be right there, so wait. One more question: are you a Master, or are you Sakura's big brother?"
"What kind of joke is that? I'm a Master, and I'm a big brother she can count on. What about you, Emiya? Are you a Master, or a coward?"

page38.text:
"...Fine.
I'll fight you as a Master, Shinji."
"Yeah. But only if it comes to a fight."
I hang up the phone.
Without skipping a beat, I turn on my heel and head straight for the front door.

page39.text:
"Wait!
Are you really going alone!?"
"That's the plan. We can talk later."

page40.text:
"That's my line.
Shinji took Sakura with him because he's got something to prove.
You'll get killed if you go charging in willy-nilly. I don't know if Shinji's aware of it, but if Sakura sees that happen to you, she'll lose it. Right now, we need to consider the situation and make a plan."

page41.text:
I know that.
But I can't just sit still.
His laughing still rings in my ears.

page42.text:
"...Oh. So he wants to kill me in front of Sakura."
"Mm...I can't say for sure, but it's likely... Hey, are you all right? You look calm, but are you actually about to fly off the handle?"

page43.text:
Fly off the handle?
She's asking me if all I can think of is running to school and punching Shinji in the face.
In that case...

page44.text:
"Yeah, I'm about to lose it. I can't think of anything else. I'm pissed at myself for not saying a damn thing this entire time, just because they're siblings.
He isn't Sakura's brother. And I let him take Sakura away."

page45.text: "I'm going to take her back. Don't get involved, Tohsaka."

page46.text:
I go outside.
The sky above is dark, and the sun's starting to set.
It's definitely going to rain tonight.
I need to bring Sakura back with me before then.
